issues.display_title: Issue #2023: Investigate and audit payment failure rate and telemetry discrepancies on Countly vs database logs (Last 60 Days)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

An analysis of payment telemetry in Countly (https://data.gothru.org) across the last 60 days (Aug 09 – Oct 07, 2026) revealed an unexpectedly low overall payment completion rate (~69.87% clean production success rate, with 182 recorded payment failures).

Initial telemetry inspection identified significant anomalies, including a high volume of failure events recorded on Countly (e.g. 2026-09-02 with 69 raw events, 36 of which were development sandbox tests and 33 were production events). Cross-referencing against production database tables (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe and ccdb.cc_logs_paypal) showed only 4 Stripe failed charges and 0 PayPal failed charges logged on that date, indicating a discrepancy between client-side Countly event triggers and authoritative database payment records.

Objectives

  1. Investigate the discrepancy between Countly payment_failed telemetry and backend ledger/log entries (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe, ccdb.cc_logs_paypal, ccdb.cc_purchase).
  2. Audit payment failure root causes in production, specifically:
    • Recurring renewal drops on Stripe (predominantly sub_pro subscriptions).
    • PayPal transaction drop-off rate compared to Stripe.
    • Moderation payment event drop-offs on 2026-09-02.
  3. Ensure server-side payment failure tracking reliably logs error response messages, failure codes, and environment segmentation to prevent telemetry pollution from sandbox/dev testing.
  4. Formulate actionable fixes for payment gateway failure handling and renewal cron reliability.

Telemetry Summary (60 Days Clean Production)

  • Total Transaction Attempts: 604
  • Payment Completed: 422 (69.87%)
  • Payment Failed: 182 (30.13%)
  • Provider Performance:
    • Stripe: 366 completed / 134 failed (73.20% success rate)
    • PayPal: 56 completed / 48 failed (53.85% success rate)
  • Top Failed Payment Types: subscription (112), moderation (20), token (16), overlay (12)
  • Top Failed Subscription Plan: sub_pro (90)

Scope of Work

  • Audit server logs (apil-1, apil-2) and database records (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe, ccdb.cc_logs_paypal) around peak failure dates.
  • Inspect Stripe Recurring Cronjob (RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper.php) error logs and failure handling.
  • Inspect PayPal Webhook / Capture failure handlers and response tracking.
  • Document findings and recommendations in docs/investigations/.

Result

The forensic investigation and telemetry audit have been completed. The full comprehensive report, detailed root cause breakdown, and actionable engineering recommendations are documented in:

  • docs/investigations/2026-10-07-payment-failure-comprehensive-audit.md

issues.display_title: Issue #2026: fix(payment): resolve stuck tour deactivation and audit overlay unlock data discrepancy for moderation 3062100
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Resolved an issue where hosted virtual tour jsn73hDg (Moderation ID: 3062100, User: 26111) remained deactivated despite the user completing a $35 overlay renewal payment on 2026-08-28.

Cause

  1. Post-Payment Crash: When the user paid, the transaction succeeded in Stripe, but the backend process encountered an error during invoice generation due to a missing billing address. This interrupted the automated tour activation step.
  2. Incomplete Data Update: While the overlay audit record was subsequently created with a valid license, the main tour table was not updated, leaving the tour marked as deactivated.
  3. Dashboard Activation Limitation: Toggling the tour active in the dashboard did not fully reset internal deactivation flags, causing the tour to remain suppressed in system queries.

Resolution & Verification

  • Code Fix: Resolved the invoice generation issue (commit 9bebff707) to ensure missing billing addresses do not interrupt post-payment processes.
  • Database Restoration: Fully restored tour jsn73hDg in the tours table (foverlay_active = 1, deactivated = 0, and cleared deactivation flags).
  • Future Deactivation Prevention: Confirmed the license is valid through 2027-08-29 in overlay_audit, ensuring automated background monitor sweeps will not deactivate the tour.
  • Scope Verification: Audited related database records and confirmed no other tours are stuck in this state.

  • Response indicates the billing collection method.

issues.display_title: Issue #2028: [Investigate] Virtual Tour Activation Failure After Transfer Due to Mismatched Moderation in overlay_audit
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Investigate an issue where a virtual tour fails to activate from the dashboard UI after the tour was transferred to another account, even though payment data was updated manually.

Investigation Scope

  • Trace the virtual tour activation flow on the backend.
  • Investigate why the system does not recognize the tour's payment status when activated from the UI.
  • Identify data requirements and mismatches preventing successful activation.

Result

The investigation found that the root cause was located in the overlay_audit table (hosted_tours.overlay_audit).

Findings:

  1. When activating a virtual tour, the system verifies payment in overlay_audit by matching both tour_key and moderation_id.
  2. Following the tour transfer, the audit record (e.g. record ID 3593784) was still referencing the previous/original moderation ID rather than the new moderation ID of the transferred tour.
  3. Because the moderation_id in overlay_audit did not match the current moderation ID being activated, the system treated the tour as unpaid and blocked the activation.

Investigation Scope

    • Examine how GetSubStatus.php queries Stripe and PayPal subscriptions.
    • Investigate why the endpoint returns subscription: true and a valid nextPayment date regardless of whether the subscription is active, past_due, unpaid, or canceled.
  2. Subscription Lifecycle & Database State:
    • Investigate whether the GoThru database (gothru_mod.users / user_extra_data) is informed or updated when Stripe webhooks / dunning cycles emit invoice payment failures (invoice.payment_failed / subscription status changes).
    • Trace how inactive subscriptions are represented across DB tables versus actual Stripe/PayPal status.
  3. Guard Logic in Plan Change Handlers:
    • Review pre-condition validation in Upgrade.php, Downgrade.php, and PaymentHelpers.php.
    • Identify where and when subscription health should be evaluated before attempting modifications.
  4. Error Handling & Localization Audit:
    • Trace why messages.tours.subscription_not_active is thrown as a raw key and why DowngradeHelper logs from: unknown when Stripe retrieval fails.

Deliverables

  • A comprehensive investigation summary detailing the state flow between Stripe/PayPal, the DB, and the API endpoints.
  • Technical recommendations and action items for gating plan change requests when subscription status is not active.

issues.display_title: Issue #1296: Add Reason Field to Street View Account Check Response
issues.main_description_html:
get /users/check-google-account
new response:
reason: "TOKEN_INVALID" | "MISSING_SCOPE"

Context

When the app checks whether a user's Google Street View account is still working, it currently only answers with "yes it works" or "no it does not work." It does not say why it does not work.

There are two different reasons an account can stop working:

  1. The connection has expired or been cut off — Google no longer recognises the account's link to the app. The user needs to connect the account again from the beginning.
  2. A required permission was removed — The account is still linked, but it no longer has the right to publish Street View photos. The user needs to give the app that permission again.

These two situations look the same to the app right now. To fix this, the check result needs to include a short label that tells the app exactly which problem occurred — so the app can show the right message and guide the user to the right solution.

Expected Result

After this change, the account check will always include a short label explaining the outcome:

  • Account is working fine — no label is included, everything is good.
  • Connection has expired or been cut off — a label is included indicating the connection problem, so the app can tell the user to reconnect their account.
  • Required permission is missing — a label is included indicating the permission problem, so the app can tell the user to grant the correct permission again.

The rest of the information returned by the check stays exactly the same. Only this extra label is added.

Acceptance Criteria

  • When the account is working fine, no problem label is included in the check result.
  • When the account's connection to Google has expired or been cut off, a label is included that identifies it as a connection problem, along with the message "Token is invalid."
  • When the account is connected but the Street View publishing permission is missing, a label is included that identifies it as a permission problem, along with the message "Token is valid, but streetviewpublish scope is missing."
  • The label is always included in the check result — it is blank when everything is fine, and filled in with the problem type when something is wrong.
  • Everything else the check returns today remains unchanged.
  • There are two defined problem labels for now: connection problem and permission problem. If any other unexpected issue occurs, it is treated as a connection problem by default.

issues.display_title: Issue #1731: feat(paypal): log every one-time payment capture
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

A capture that succeeds at PayPal but fails to fulfil leaves no trace anywhere in our systems:

  • grep -rn "Log::" app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/ returns nothing
  • grep -rni "webhook" routes/ app/Http/Controllers/Payment returns nothing
  • HelperClass::responseMessages() (HelperClass.php:663) only builds a response array, it does not log
  • CCTrans and CCLog rows are only inserted inside process*Success(), which never runs on a failure

CreateOrder writes nothing to the database either, so an order that is created and then abandoned or failed leaves no record at all. What remains is an entry in the PayPal dashboard with no way to match it back to a user, tour or moderation.

Change

  • Log every one-time payment capture with the PayPal order id, capture id, amount, user_id, product_name and outcome.
  • Log the failure path explicitly, including the reason fulfilment was refused and whether a refund was attempted.
  • Follow up separately with a PayPal webhook so captures are reconciled even when our response never reaches the client. Until that exists the log is the only recovery path.

Acceptance

test_a_capture_that_cannot_be_fulfilled_leaves_a_trace in tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/CaptureOrderBindingTest.php goes from red to green. It spies the log and asserts an error is recorded when fulfilment fails after a successful capture.

Files

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/CaptureOrder.php
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/CaptureOverlayOrder.php
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/CreateOrder.php
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/CreateOverlayOrder.php

Result — 2026-08-03

Implemented in #1740 (feat/paypal-onetime-capture-logging, commits 28a88cc9a + 84d82dbbf).

  • CaptureOrder / CaptureOverlayOrder: log every capture with order_id, capture_id, amount, user_id, product_name, and outcome. Outcome is success, capture_failed (PayPal never completed the capture), or fulfilment_failed (capture succeeded but fulfilment threw) — failure logs also include reason and refund_attempted.
  • CreateOrder / CreateOverlayOrder: log order creation (order_id, user_id, product_name, amount) and a failure log with reason when creation fails.
  • Code review on #1740 caught the new logging sitting inside the same try block that triggers a refund on failure — a logging outage could turn an already-fulfilled purchase into a bogus refund. Fixed by routing all new log calls through PaypalHelper::safeLog(), which swallows logging failures instead of letting them escape into the caller.
  • Webhook-based reconciliation stays out of scope, tracked separately per the original issue.

Tests: tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/CaptureOrderBindingTest.php (15 tests) and tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/CreateOrderTest.php (5 tests), including test_a_capture_that_cannot_be_fulfilled_leaves_a_trace, log-content assertions for both outcomes, and a regression test proving a logging failure no longer triggers a refund or a false error response.

Background

In #1820, multi-level menu hierarchies (sub > sub > sub) were flattened into a 1D sub array in GET /templates/menu/match (V1) to prevent legacy frontend crashes. A V2 endpoint is required to natively return the fully recursive nested tree structure.

Scope & Tasks

  1. New Route: Add GET /v2/templates/menu/match.
  2. Recursive Parser: Use OverlaysClass::getMenuV2() to build multi-level nested structures (name, pano_id, recursive sub_menus).
  3. Recursive Validation: Recursively validate panorama IDs against tablePanoramas while preserving structural containers (pano_id = 0).
  4. Backward Compatibility: Ensure the V1 endpoint remains unchanged with its 1D flattened structure.

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /v2/templates/menu/match returns fully nested menu trees.
  • Language fallback remains safe ($lang -> 'en' -> '').

    • Decomposed legacy fat controller into single-action controllers:
      • GetServicesController (GET /photographers/services)
      • GetListServicesController (GET /photographers/services/list)
      • DeleteServiceController (DELETE /photographers/services/delete/{serviceId})
    • Route definitions in routes/photographerRoutes.php updated under photographers/services prefix and auth middleware.
    • Controllers coordinate dedicated actions: GetServicesAction, GetListServicesAction, DeleteServiceAction.
    • Superuser impersonation (?sid=) reinstated on GetServicesController via SuperUserHelper::isSuperUser((int) $userId).
    • Actions delegate HTTP transport to PhotographerServicesService with client IP forwarding.
    • Error & Domain Code Mapping:
      • ServicesFetchFailedException mapped to HTTP 422 (PHOTOGRAPHERS.SERVICES_FETCH_FAILED).
      • ServiceDeleteFailedException mapped to HTTP 409 (PHOTOGRAPHERS.SERVICE_DELETE_FAILED).
      • Handled cleanly via PhotographersExceptionHttpMapper.
